title: A mountain temple
translation: If you shut yourself away in a mountain temple and serve the Buddha, you're never bored, and your mind feels like it's been rinsed clean.
original: {山寺|やまでら}にかきこもりて、{仏|ほとけ}に{仕|つか}うまつるこそ、つれづれもなく、{心|こころ}の{濁|にご}りもきよまる{心地|ここち}すれ。
literal: Shutting oneself up in a mountain temple and serving the Buddha: that gives a feeling of having no tedium, and of the muddiness of the heart being cleansed.

notes.text: The same つれづれ as in the first words of the book: the long, empty hours. Here he names something that cures them.
'The muddiness of the heart': worldly desires, {煩悩|ぼんなう} in Buddhist terms. The 1925 edition glosses it exactly so.
